dedupe_keys.name: colosseum o ran commag slicing and scheduling experiment data

description: This dataset records radio-access experiments used to study learning-based slicing and scheduling in the Colosseum wireless emulator. The WI NES Lab team publishes CSV measurements, trained agents and an example loader for four base stations, 40 user devices and three slices per station. The documented channel is 3 MHz with 15 physical resource blocks. Scenarios vary user distance, static or 3 m/s mobility, traffic class and round-robin, waterfilling or proportionally fair scheduling. Coverage is the emulated Rome radio scenario, not a field census; collection dates are not stated. Resource allocations change in documented 30-second stages over an eight-minute schedule. Public GitHub access is free under the repository’s GPL version 3 licence. A limitation is that real-time deployment requires users to implement data collection and feedback functions. The granted-to-requested resource ratio is a latency-related reward proxy, not directly measured delay. Simulation uses include replaying slice performance and comparing allocation policies. It relates to platform-colosseum-open-ran-digital-twin as the experiment environment. CSV contents, agent archives and code execution were not tested.
